about: POST /scim and GET /scim/limits. Recorded against the api as it was before the family switched to the model (docs/v0.9.5/data-model.md). Every target is scim.invalid, which RFC 6761 guarantees never resolves, so a well-formed request ends in the same 502 on any machine. The request size cap (scimMaxRequestBytes, 1 MiB) is not recorded here: a body past it would make this file a megabyte; tests/scim_protocol.js drives it.

cases.name: scim: an empty body is refused for its url

body.error: url is required. It is the ABSOLUTE URL of the SCIM endpoint — the service root plus the path, as the page composes it (for example https://host/scim/v2/Users?count=10).

cases.name: scim: an empty url is refused

body.error: url is required. It is the ABSOLUTE URL of the SCIM endpoint — the service root plus the path, as the page composes it (for example https://host/scim/v2/Users?count=10).

cases.name: scim: a relative url is refused

body.error: url must be an absolute http:// or https:// URL. A relative one has no host for this service to resolve, and resolving it against this service's own address would make this endpoint a way to reach the api's own routes.

cases.name: scim: a url that is not a string
cases.changed: The model types url as a string or null and refuses anything else naming the member. Until then the proxy stringified a number and refused "5" as a relative URL, which named the wrong problem.

body.error: url must be an absolute http:// or https:// URL. A relative one has no host for this service to resolve, and resolving it against this service's own address would make this endpoint a way to reach the api's own routes.
Refusing the request: `url` must be a JSON string or null. GET /api-docs describes what scimCall takes.

cases.name: scim: a method outside the protocol's is refused

body.error: method must be one of GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE. RFC 7644 uses exactly those five, and forwarding an arbitrary method would make this endpoint useful for something other than SCIM.

cases.name: scim: headers that are not an object
cases.changed: headers is an object or null in the model, so an array is refused naming the member. Until then the proxy refused it with its own sentence; the refusal is the same, only its words and code are the model's.

body.error: headers must be an object of name to value.
Refusing the request: `headers` must be a JSON object or null. GET /api-docs describes what scimCall takes.

cases.name: scim: a header name that is not a token is refused

body.error: The header name "Bad Name" is not a token (RFC 7230 section 3.2.6), so it is not a header name at all.

cases.name: scim: a framing header is refused

body.error: This endpoint will not forward the Host header. It would send the request to a different virtual host than the URL names, which is how a proxy is turned into an open one. Everything else is forwarded as sent — the refusals here are about the SHAPE of the request rather than its content.

cases.name: scim: a CR/LF in a header value is refused

body.error: The value of X-Note contains a carriage return or a line feed. That is header injection rather than a header value, and it is refused before it is anything else.

cases.name: scim: a body on a GET is refused

body.error: A GET carries no body in RFC 7644, and this endpoint refuses one rather than dropping it — a body that is silently discarded is how the wrong method goes unnoticed. A query by POST is what /.search is for.

cases.name: scim: a body on a DELETE is refused

body.error: A DELETE carries no body in RFC 7644, and this endpoint refuses one rather than dropping it — a body that is silently discarded is how the wrong method goes unnoticed. A query by POST is what /.search is for.

cases.name: scim: a well-formed GET reaches the network (a name that cannot resolve)

body.error: The SCIM server could not be reached: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND scim.invalid

cases.name: scim: a well-formed POST reaches the network, with its trace

body.error: The SCIM server could not be reached: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND scim.invalid

cases.name: scim: a PATCH whose body is already text

body.error: The SCIM server could not be reached: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND scim.invalid

refusedHeaderReasons.host: It would send the request to a different virtual host than the URL names, which is how a proxy is turned into an open one.
refusedHeaderReasons.content-length: The body framing is this service's to set — a caller that could set it could smuggle a second request inside the first.
refusedHeaderReasons.transfer-encoding: Body framing again, and the other half of the same smuggling pair.
refusedHeaderReasons.connection: Hop-by-hop (RFC 7230 section 6.1). It belongs to the connection this service opens, not to the request being carried.
refusedHeaderReasons.upgrade: Hop-by-hop, and it asks to stop speaking HTTP.
refusedHeaderReasons.proxy-authorization: It authenticates to a proxy rather than to the SCIM server, so forwarding it would send this service's hop credentials somewhere they do not belong.

body.addressPolicy: The same one every outbound call from this service obeys: api/ssrf_guard.js, installed on the shared axios instance, so loopback and private ranges are refused on the request AND on any redirect into one. It is not re-implemented here.
body.statusRule: A refusal by this service is a 400; a network failure is a 502; and a SCIM error from the far end is a 200 carrying that status and its scimType. A 409 uniqueness, a 404, a 403 and the 501 on /Me are the server ANSWERING, and reporting them as failures would make this endpoint unable to show the errors it exists to show.
body.whatThisIsNot: Not a general HTTP proxy. Five methods, no body on a GET or a DELETE, and the framing headers are refused.
